A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAITHCOT-BENCH and FINE-COT. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original expert annotations, analyses of generated reasoning traces, and evaluations of eleven detectors across four datasets, including full results in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds correlation and mutual-information estimates derived from the benchmark annotations in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, two-category/eight-signal taxonomy, annotation procedure, and detection task are retained. Expanded detector descriptions in Appendix C.1 and proposed future training strategies do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use LogiQA, TruthfulQA, AQuA, and HLE-Bio, retaining the same domains, difficulty analyses, and distribution-shift scenarios. Appendix B.1 analyzes existing instances rather than extending coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain Random, Perplexity, five counterfactual variants, Answer Tracing, Information Gain, Step-Judge, and Faithful-Judge. Appendix C.1 expands their descriptions without establishing a replacement or newly evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The 378-query collection, four generator models, annotation workflow, prompts, and detector metrics remain unchanged. Table 1's GPT-4o-to-GPT-4o-mini relabeling aligns with both versions' existing model setup; it does not establish a model substitution.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.1 quantifies the association between correctness and faithfulness using the existing Figure 6a counts. This supplements the earlier distribution analysis; the difficulty, distribution-shift, subtype, and example analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 introduces phi-correlation and mutual-information estimation from the binary contingency counts. Annotation-agreement reporting is unchanged, and neither version provides detector repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports phi = 0.286 and mutual information = 0.057 for 1,183 instances in Appendix B.1. The numerical benchmark results in Tables 1–3 and existing figure statistics remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds specific mathematical definitions for answer-confidence increments and question-conditioned information gain, including a token-probability expansion in Equations 13–15. V1 supplied only qualitative descriptions. The central task definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, annotated-dataset contribution, eleven-method evaluation, and principal findings. The added conclusion sentence reiterates the existing distinction between apparent transparency and faithful reasoning.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly identifies mechanistic validation of observable faithfulness signals as future work, discusses balancing accuracy and faithfulness, and proposes evaluation beyond binary labels. Appendix B.1 additionally interprets correctness–faithfulness association as weak.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 provides additional computational detail through perturbation/model-call notation, probability conversion, and detector-scoring expressions. Dataset setup and prompts are unchanged. The code URL added to the abstract already appeared in v1's reproducibility statement.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including Matton et al., Tutek et al., Goldowsky-Dill et al., and Hong and Roth, while removing Lou et al. and two Tan et al. references. The related-work organization and instance-level benchmark positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Future Work section and Appendix B.1, expands Appendix C.1, and makes localized author-contact, header, and wording edits. Most prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: All eleven figures and three tables are retained. Changes include local reflow, Figure 4 moving from page 5 to page 6, displayed appendix equations, conference headers, and corrected GPT-4o-mini labels in Table 1.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.1 adds reproducible quantitative support for the previously qualitative correctness–faithfulness distinction, and Section 6 makes the need to validate observable signals against internal reasoning explicit. Additional detector documentation modestly improves transparency. These gains are limited: the benchmark results are unchanged, and the underlying validation gap remains unresolved.
